offer.say: Seven minutes, {owner}. Seven! I just found out. That clock's been fast since 1996. I've been showing up at the Hat Trick for the 10:45 pitcher at 10:38 for eighteen years. That's two hours a year, standing at a bar, waiting. Do you know what I could do with two hours?

options.text: I'll look into the clock.
What would you do with two hours?
It's fast so your league gets on the ice on time.
Honestly, Dwayne, it's seven minutes.

why.say: Wait at the bar for two more hours, probably. But on MY terms.

options.text: Fair. Let me look into it.

purpose.say: Oh, sure, for the hockey. We've been late for eleven games anyway. The clock didn't save us. The clock only works on people who care about the hockey. I care about the pitcher.

options.text: Okay. I'll see what can be done.

decline.say: It's seven minutes a game. That's a whole period of beer league, if you add it up. I added it up. In the bar. While I was waiting.

accepted.say: Thank you. The Ice Holes salute you. They're not here, they're at the bar, but they'd salute you.

options.text: Going to have a look at it.
I want to hear what Midge thinks.
I've made a decision about the clock.
Done. Let's see what happens at 10:45.
Just checking.
I'm setting it right. True time from now on.

do.note: The Moosebrew clock now shows the true time. Somewhere in Millbrook, someone is writing a letter.

options.text: It stays fast. It's a keepsake. But here's a watch from the lost and found, set to the real time.
It stays fast. Leave a little earlier, Dwayne.

p_right.say: TRUE TIME. You're a hero. Midge is going to write a column about you. It's going to be mean. It's going to be so well written.

p_watch.say: A watch! Somebody lost a watch at the rink and now it's mine. It's got a Big Gord's Trucks logo on it. Big Gord won't let me walk. Big Gord will let me arrive on time.

p_leave.say: Leave earlier. From a hockey game. On purpose. That's... that's actually allowed, isn't it.

p_game.say: Ten forty-five. Pitcher time. For the first time in eighteen years I'm going to see it poured.

complete.say: 10:45 on the dot. The pitcher arrived as I arrived. It was like a dance. The whole team cried. Okay, Terry from the Plungers cried, he was there for his own reasons.

options.text: Worth it?
Maybe come to more games now?
Enjoy the pitcher, Dwayne.
I set the clock right.
The watch.
I told you to leave early.

c_right.say: Worth it. The Late Ice League was four minutes late on the ice, but we were always late on the ice. Now we're late on purpose.

c_watch.say: Worth it. The clock's still fast, the town's still happy, and I've got a watch that says Big Gord on it. Everybody wins. Especially Big Gord.

c_leave.say: I left after the second period. Nobody noticed. The team was down six. Honestly, the best night of my life.

c_games.say: More games. Wow. Okay. Maybe one more. Don't tell the bar.

c_enjoy.say: I always do. Now I enjoy it on time.
